identity.purpose: Pronto is a local-first command center that helps a person understand, improve, and safely move work across a portfolio of software repositories.
audience: Repository owners who need a fast, evidence-backed explanation of unfamiliar code
Operators coordinating quality, remediation, custody, and delivery across multiple repositories
Agents preparing bounded work without inventing authority or product truth
outcomes: Understand what a repository does and how an important behavior moves through it
See which operational evidence is current, missing, blocked, or stale
Hand off an evidence-backed next action through Pronto's existing guards

actors.label: Repository reader
actors.description: Enters the city to learn its purpose, follow a journey, and inspect the evidence behind the explanation.

actors.label: Portfolio operator
actors.description: Uses quality, remediation, custody, and delivery evidence to decide what needs attention and what is ready to move.

actors.label: Guarded agent
actors.description: Receives a scoped, evidence-backed task and prepares work without bypassing repository ownership or release gates.

payloads.label: repository context
payloads.description: Workspace identity, freshness, measured topology, and source anchors move from the repository boundary into the city renderer.

payloads.label: quality evidence
payloads.description: Freshness, findings, maturity, and behavior receipts travel through Pronto without being converted into unsupported green states.

payloads.label: guarded work order
payloads.description: A scoped remediation or preparation request leaves Telescope through an existing guarded handoff rather than mutating the repository from the map.

decisions.label: Source topology stays canonical
decisions.explanation: Telescope measures code structure first; Compass, behavior, quality, remediation, and intent may annotate the city but cannot replace its source-derived topology.

decisions.label: Runtime AI is not required
decisions.explanation: The desktop app uses local deterministic projections. An agent may prepare a draft manifest ahead of time, but the app stores no model prompt or credential.

decisions.label: The city explains before it acts
decisions.explanation: Telescope remains read-only and hands source opening, remediation, and preparation to existing guarded Pronto surfaces.

failures.label: Reviewed meaning no longer matches source
failures.behavior: Pronto marks the city stale, keeps the measured preview available, and opens only the affected readiness questions instead of silently rewriting authored meaning.

failures.label: Consequential meaning is missing
failures.behavior: Pronto shows the Map Workshop and an explicitly incomplete measured preview; it does not present a polished city as complete.

failures.label: A guarded action cannot proceed
failures.behavior: The existing remediation, custody, or release surface explains the blocking evidence while Telescope remains read-only.

groups.label: Experience district
groups.summary: The open workspace where people choose a repository, inspect evidence, and move between Pronto surfaces.

groups.label: Telescope city
groups.summary: The visual explanation layer that turns measured repository structure into readable districts, buildings, rails, and flows.

groups.label: Native orchestration
groups.summary: The Tauri and Rust boundary that binds the desktop surface to registered workspaces and guarded Pronto operations.

groups.label: Evidence district
groups.summary: Quality, behavior assurance, runtime parity, and evidence contracts explain whether the repository is trustworthy and current.

groups.label: Workflow and delivery
groups.summary: Changes, custody, remediation, release rules, promotion, and task lanes carry work from a finding to a guarded delivery decision.

groups.label: Intent and automation
groups.summary: Compass, skill usage, and activity signals add operational context without redefining the source-derived architecture.

nodes.label: Workspace shell
nodes.whatItDoes: Frames the active repository and gives a person one calm place to understand what is happening.
nodes.howItsBuilt: A React application composes route surfaces, shared state, keyboard behavior, and guarded actions.

explanation.purpose: Give a repository reader one stable entrance to Pronto's portfolio, evidence, and guarded work surfaces.
explanation.userOutcome: A person can enter one repository, understand its current state, and choose a safe next action without learning Pronto's internal modules first.
triggers: A repository is selected from the portfolio
steps: Load current repository and evidence projections
Open the requested overview or Telescope surface
stateChanges: The active repository route and contextual surface change
decisions: Chooses which bounded repository surface is visible
failures: Unavailable repository snapshots remain explicit instead of rendering invented state
security: Mutation authority remains behind existing Tauri commands and guards
performance: Loads one primary workspace per route

nodes.label: Global rail
nodes.whatItDoes: Keeps portfolio, work, evidence, and configuration reachable without crowding the architecture canvas.
nodes.howItsBuilt: A compact sidebar and topbar provide stable navigation while contextual details stay in drawers.

nodes.label: Detail drawer
nodes.whatItDoes: Opens focused repository detail without making every explanation persist on screen.
nodes.howItsBuilt: The drawer composes repository surfaces and hands Telescope a selected repository snapshot.

nodes.label: Telescope surface
nodes.whatItDoes: Lets anyone follow a repository story from a district overview into source evidence.
nodes.howItsBuilt: A React Flow viewport coordinates scene layout, synchronized selection, level of detail, flow tokens, and workflow lenses.

explanation.purpose: Turn source-backed architecture and behavior into a guided city that an unfamiliar reader can explore.
explanation.userOutcome: A person can explain the repository's purpose, major areas, an important action, and the evidence behind it.
triggers: A district or building is selected
steps: Enter one building for local evidence
stateChanges: Selection, scope, lens, and tour stop update without altering topology
boundaries: No source bodies in the projection
decisions: Overview, district, and building scopes use different semantic projections
security: Guarded tasks and source opening hand off to existing Pronto surfaces
performance: Source detail renders one building and immediate handoffs only
testing: Scope, selection, keyboard, reduced-motion, and source-detail tests

nodes.label: City silhouettes
nodes.whatItDoes: Uses recognizable building forms to make routes, stores, interfaces, services, and integrations legible before labels are read.
nodes.howItsBuilt: Custom SVG primitives render fin rows, towers, slab stacks, cubes, and low slabs inside React Flow nodes.

nodes.label: Scene model
nodes.whatItDoes: Chooses what belongs in the overview, subsystem, and source views while keeping every building traceable.
nodes.howItsBuilt: Deterministic bucketing compacts measured nodes, preserves authored buildings, and marks the primary story flow.

explanation.purpose: Project the same canonical architecture into a whole-city overview, a district interior, or one building's local handoffs.
explanation.userOutcome: Changing detail level reveals new information instead of shrinking the same global graph.
steps: Aggregate measured nodes into authored buildings
Build typed rails and primary story identity
boundaries: Does not invent actors or payloads
decisions: Semantic scope replaces arbitrary building quotas
failures: Missing selection falls back to the primary high-confidence story
performance: Building source detail is local by construction
testing: Adaptive overview and local source-scope fixtures

nodes.label: District layout
nodes.whatItDoes: Places neighborhoods and routes so the city remains open, readable, and stable across refreshes.
nodes.howItsBuilt: A dependency-light grid and dimetric projection pack buildings, preserve spacing, and route rails around silhouettes.

nodes.label: Telescope contract
nodes.whatItDoes: Carries measured topology, authored meaning, provenance, freshness, and privacy-safe source handoffs to the UI.
nodes.howItsBuilt: Typed projection interfaces make narrative status, coverage, visual overrides, rails, and flows explicit.

nodes.label: Repository extractor
nodes.whatItDoes: Measures the active worktree so the city remains tied to real files, relationships, freshness, and coverage.
nodes.howItsBuilt: Rust adapters inspect supported source files, fall back to generic topology, and overlay the authored map without rewriting it.

explanation.purpose: Measure the active worktree and reconcile it with reviewed repository meaning without overwriting authorship.
explanation.userOutcome: Every city claim can be traced to current source, reviewed meaning, or an explicit unknown.
stateChanges: Cache entries change only when the workspace fingerprint or visual model changes
boundaries: No source bodies, diffs, prompts, answers, or absolute personal paths enter the cache
decisions: Readiness is categorical, not a blended score
failures: Fingerprint drift makes reviewed meaning stale
security: AI is not called by the app runtime
performance: Expensive extraction and layout remain outside the full render path
testing: Readiness, privacy, cache, language, drift, and deterministic ID fixtures

nodes.label: Desktop boundary
nodes.whatItDoes: Connects the desktop shell to the repository registry, guarded commands, and local evidence surfaces.
nodes.howItsBuilt: Tauri commands and Rust modules expose typed read-only projections while keeping mutation behind existing gates.

nodes.label: Repository core
nodes.whatItDoes: Resolves registered repositories and supplies the workspace context that every Telescope answer needs.
nodes.howItsBuilt: A Rust core owns repository snapshots, command routing, and the bridge to the Telescope generator.

nodes.label: Quality runner
nodes.whatItDoes: Shows which quality dimensions, checks, and findings affect a building or rail.
nodes.howItsBuilt: Quality projections preserve freshness, detector coverage, maturity, and installed-runtime evidence states.

nodes.label: Behavior assurance
nodes.whatItDoes: Separates verified behavior from assumptions so an attractive map cannot imply unsupported certainty.
nodes.howItsBuilt: Repository contracts and receipts feed explicit verified, stale, unavailable, partial, and conflicted states.

nodes.label: Remediation plans
nodes.whatItDoes: Attaches current blockers, actions, dependencies, and closure evidence to the architecture involved.
nodes.howItsBuilt: Remediation projections overlay source-bound findings and hand actions off to guarded preparation surfaces.

nodes.label: Custody lanes
nodes.whatItDoes: Makes active work, ownership, and safe integration paths visible without guessing from prompts or filenames.
nodes.howItsBuilt: Custody records and workspace evidence drive changes and ownership overlays with explicit verification boundaries.

nodes.label: Release gates
nodes.whatItDoes: Shows the path from changed subsystem through checks and release rules to a ship-ready decision.
nodes.howItsBuilt: Release boundary checks consume repository evidence and preserve blocked, stale, and unavailable outcomes.

nodes.label: Compass intent
nodes.whatItDoes: Adds goals, blockers, and drift context to the architecture without becoming the source of its topology.
nodes.howItsBuilt: Project Compass remains an optional adapter projected as a lens over source-derived districts and flows.

nodes.label: Verified automation
nodes.whatItDoes: Explains which agent or skill activity is verified and where recurring automation friction is accumulating.
nodes.howItsBuilt: Skill usage and papercut collectors provide evidence-bound activity overlays rather than inferred activity.

actions.label: Open a repository
actions.whatItDoes: Moves from the portfolio into the selected repository workspace and its visual explanation.
actions.howItsBuilt: The global shell opens a repository drawer and hands the registered workspace to the repository surface.

explanation.purpose: Give an unfamiliar reader a reliable mental model of Pronto before they have to read its source.
explanation.userOutcome: The reader can name Pronto's purpose, its major districts, one important workflow, and the evidence behind that explanation.
triggers: A reader asks how Pronto works
preconditions: The active worktree has been measured
steps: Check whether the city is reviewed or still needs information
Inspect a district or building for implementation evidence
stateChanges: The current city scope and selection change; repository source does not
responsibilities: Keep authored meaning separate from measured facts
Expose evidence and uncertainty at every level
boundaries: Telescope explains and routes; guarded Pronto surfaces own mutations
decisions: Incomplete meaning opens the Map Workshop instead of masquerading as a finished city
failures: Extraction failure makes the map unavailable
Source drift makes reviewed narrative stale
security: Cached projections exclude source bodies, diffs, prompts, and absolute personal paths
performance: Each exploration level renders only its semantic scope
testing: An unfamiliar-reader test must recover purpose, major areas, one action, evidence, and one operational concern

actions.label: Understand this repository
actions.whatItDoes: Starts with the repository story and reveals how Pronto turns source evidence into an explorable city.
actions.howItsBuilt: The drawer, Telescope surface, and versioned projection contract form the read-only handoff.

actions.label: Explore the architecture
actions.whatItDoes: Shows the repository as neighborhoods, buildings, rails, and flows that can be explored at several levels of detail.
actions.howItsBuilt: The authored scene model and deterministic layout transform measured nodes into a responsive visual city.

actions.label: Find an action
actions.whatItDoes: Searches the canonical action projection and focuses the city on the behavior or workflow you want to understand.
actions.howItsBuilt: The renderer filters backend actions, resolves their mapped nodes and rails, and leaves the full city available underneath the focus.

actions.label: Inspect source evidence
actions.whatItDoes: Explains which source files and relationships support a building, rail, flow, or action.
actions.howItsBuilt: Repository-relative anchors, symbols, provenance, and confidence travel with the projection without caching source bodies.

explanation.purpose: Let a reader verify a city claim without turning the entire repository into an unreadable dependency graph.
explanation.userOutcome: The reader can trace the selected building to its local handoffs, symbols, files, and claim-level provenance.
triggers: A district, building, rail, flow, or action is selected
preconditions: The selected entity has repository-relative evidence
steps: Inspect its immediate incoming and outgoing handoffs
Open a source anchor through the guarded workspace handoff
stateChanges: Only the visual scope and progressive evidence expansion change
responsibilities: Keep evidence local to the selected building
boundaries: The projection stores paths and symbols, not source bodies
decisions: Unrelated repository entities are hidden until the reader navigates to them
failures: Unsupported relationships remain partial or inferred
security: No source bodies, diffs, or runtime payload values enter the Telescope cache
performance: Evidence is virtualized or progressively expanded and the graph stays one-hop local
testing: Stress the prior global-source-graph crash shape and prove the source scope remains bounded

actions.label: Refresh the workspace map
actions.whatItDoes: Regenerates the city from the active worktree so the map is bound to the current commit and dirty-state fingerprint.
actions.howItsBuilt: Telescope extraction runs through the Tauri and CLI projection boundary with cooperative cancellation and cache replacement.

actions.label: Audit behavior assurance
actions.whatItDoes: Shows which declared behaviors are missing evidence and keeps assurance gaps from becoming a ready claim.
actions.howItsBuilt: The action is backed by the repository-owned v2 behavior contract and Quality Runner's replay-verified projection.

actions.label: Inspect behavior evidence
actions.whatItDoes: Separates contract, profile, result, freshness, verification, and release state for the selected behavior.
actions.howItsBuilt: The behavior assurance projection links immutable receipts and bounded scenario coverage without exposing sensitive traces.

actions.label: Check release assurance
actions.whatItDoes: Explains whether release preparation is blocked by a missing, stale, failed, or insufficient behavior receipt.
actions.howItsBuilt: The release boundary consumes the same Tier-0 behavior assurance state rather than maintaining a second gate.

actions.label: Inspect assurance across the portfolio
actions.whatItDoes: Compares release assurance with all-tier edge durability without treating either view as a generic green score.
actions.howItsBuilt: Quality workspace projections preserve the behavior assurance taxonomy and bounded repository filters.

actions.label: Review workspace custody
actions.whatItDoes: Shows the evidence and safe next step for active, dirty, stale, or unavailable workspaces before any guarded handoff.
actions.howItsBuilt: Custody receipts and live Git state project into Pronto as read-only lanes with granular dispositions.

actions.label: Review service lifecycle safety
actions.whatItDoes: Explains whether a routine update can restart a loaded service safely or requires an explicit registration path.
actions.howItsBuilt: The behavior contract and lifecycle tests distinguish unchanged, missing, and materially changed LaunchAgents.

actions.label: See what changed
actions.whatItDoes: Focuses the city on dirty workspaces, branch movement, and integration paths that may affect the repository story.
actions.howItsBuilt: Changes and custody remain an overlay over source-derived nodes; they do not rewrite the architecture.

actions.label: Work the remediation plan
actions.whatItDoes: Shows the architecture involved in current remediation actions, blockers, dependencies, and closure evidence.
actions.howItsBuilt: Remediation remains a guarded Pronto handoff; the city only filters and explains affected source-backed areas.

explanation.purpose: Explain where a remediation plan touches the architecture and what prevents the work from closing.
explanation.userOutcome: The operator can see affected facilities, blocking dependencies, custody, and required closure evidence in one city story.
triggers: A Telescope readiness gap is routed into remediation
stateChanges: Telescope does not change remediation status; the owning guarded workflow does
responsibilities: Preserve the canonical remediation task state
Report unmapped actions rather than inventing locations
boundaries: The lens annotates canonical topology and never creates a second task database
decisions: Only source-mapped facilities receive repair crews or blocked-route visuals
failures: Stale or unmapped remediation evidence remains visible and unconfirmed
security: The city receives task metadata and anchors, not sensitive worktree content
performance: The lens filters the unchanged city rather than generating another topology
testing: Lens isolation and unmapped-information reporting are required

actions.label: Prepare delivery
actions.whatItDoes: Explains the path from changed subsystem through validation and release rules without claiming that preparation has run.
actions.howItsBuilt: The delivery lens connects repository evidence, custody, release gates, and guarded preparation surfaces.

explanation.purpose: Show how a change moves from an owned workspace through validation to a release decision.
explanation.userOutcome: The operator can locate the changed subsystem, understand its gates, and see the exact blocker before preparing delivery.
triggers: A delivery action or lens is selected
preconditions: Changed facilities and release evidence can be mapped
stateChanges: The city selection changes; no release action runs inside Telescope
responsibilities: Keep source state, installed state, and release evidence distinct
Do not imply a gate passed when evidence is missing
boundaries: Release preparation remains owned by Pronto's existing guarded surface
decisions: Unmapped checks are reported instead of receiving decorative checkpoints
failures: Missing, stale, failed, or insufficient evidence blocks the story before the release terminal
security: No diffs or runtime payload values are copied into the city projection
performance: The lens activates only facilities on the delivery path
testing: Verify the changed-subsystem-to-release route and all unavailable states

actions.label: Open source workspace
actions.whatItDoes: Hands a selected source anchor to the existing editor surface for direct inspection.
actions.howItsBuilt: Telescope preserves repository-relative evidence and delegates opening to the guarded Pronto workspace handoff.

actions.label: Preview an AI summary
actions.whatItDoes: Shows an optional repository-scoped summary while preserving the difference between inference and confirmed source evidence.
actions.howItsBuilt: AI enrichment remains disabled by default and is mediated by the existing permission and preview boundary.
